title: Duplicate charges
text: If you see two charges for the same billing period, the second is almost always a pending authorization that your bank will release within 3-5 business days. If both charges settle, reply with the last four digits of the card and both transaction dates and we will refund the duplicate within one business day. Duplicate charges do not affect your subscription status.

title: Refund policy
text: Monthly plans are refundable within 14 days of the charge. Annual plans are refundable pro rata within 30 days of purchase; after 30 days, cancellation stops the next renewal but the current term is not refunded. Refunds go back to the original payment method and take 5-10 business days to appear. Requests outside these windows require a billing specialist review.

title: Downloading invoices
text: Workspace owners and billing admins can download any invoice from Settings > Billing > Invoice history. Each invoice is available as PDF and includes your VAT ID and billing address as set at the time of the charge. Invoices are generated within an hour of a successful payment. Members without the billing role cannot see this page.

title: Updating your payment method
text: Go to Settings > Billing > Payment method and choose Replace card. The new card is verified with a zero-amount authorization and becomes the default immediately. If a renewal already failed, click Retry payment after updating; the workspace stays active for a 7-day grace period.

title: Cancelling a subscription
text: Cancel from Settings > Billing > Plan > Cancel plan. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the current term and the workspace moves to the free tier with read-only access to existing data. Annual subscriptions cannot be cancelled mid-term for a refund without a specialist review; see the refund policy.

title: Sales tax and VAT
text: We charge VAT or sales tax based on the billing address. VAT-registered businesses in the EU and UK can be zero-rated under the reverse-charge mechanism by adding a valid VAT ID in Settings > Billing > Tax details before the next invoice. Past invoices cannot be re-issued automatically; tax corrections require a billing specialist.

title: Promotion and discount codes
text: Promo codes are entered on the checkout page before confirming the plan. Codes are case-insensitive, single-use per workspace, and cannot be combined. A code shows as invalid if it has expired, was already redeemed by the workspace, or applies to a different plan tier than the one selected.

title: Two-factor codes rejected
text: Authenticator codes are time-based and drift by more than 30 seconds will cause every code to be rejected. Enable automatic time sync on the phone, then in the authenticator app use the time-correction option. If codes still fail, sign in with a recovery code and re-enroll the authenticator from Settings > Security.

title: Recovery codes
text: Ten single-use recovery codes are generated when two-factor is enabled and can be regenerated from Settings > Security > Recovery codes. Each code works once. If you have no recovery codes and no access to your authenticator, another workspace admin can temporarily disable 2FA on your account from the Members page.

title: Account recovery when locked out
text: If you are the sole admin and have lost both your authenticator and recovery codes, account recovery requires identity verification by our security team. Submit a request from the login page using Can't access your account; expect a response within two business days. We cannot bypass 2FA over chat or email.

title: Setting up SAML single sign-on
text: SAML SSO is available on Business and Enterprise plans. Configure your identity provider with the ACS URL and entity ID shown in Settings > Security > SSO, then upload the IdP metadata XML. Enable Test mode first so admins can verify sign-in before enforcing SSO for all members.

title: SSO redirect loops and assertion errors
text: A redirect loop after IdP login usually means the SAML response is rejected: most commonly an expired IdP signing certificate, a NameID format other than email, or a clock skew above 5 minutes. Check the SSO audit log for the rejection reason. Certificate rotations on the IdP side must be re-uploaded in Settings > Security > SSO.

title: Password reset emails
text: Reset emails come from no-reply@ and can take up to 10 minutes. If nothing arrives, check that the address is the one on the account, look for a company-level quarantine, and ask your mail admin to allowlist our sending domain. Accounts that sign in with SSO or Google do not have a password to reset.

title: Requiring two-factor for all members
text: Owners on Team plans and above can require two-factor from Settings > Security > Require 2FA. Members without 2FA are prompted to enroll at next sign-in and cannot access the workspace until they do. Enforcement does not apply to members who sign in through SSO, where MFA is the identity provider's responsibility.

title: Session length and unexpected sign-outs
text: Sessions last 30 days by default; admins can shorten this in Settings > Security. Being signed out every few minutes is almost always a browser extension or privacy setting clearing cookies, or a corporate proxy that strips the session cookie. Try an incognito window with extensions disabled to isolate the cause.

title: API rate limits
text: Limits are per API key: Starter 100 req/min, Pro 300 req/min, Business 600 req/min, Enterprise custom. Burst limits are enforced over a 10-second window, so 600 req/min means 100 requests per 10 seconds, not 600 in the first second. Every response includes X-RateLimit-Remaining and Retry-After headers.

title: Configuring webhooks
text: Webhooks are configured per workspace in Settings > Developer > Webhooks. Endpoints must be HTTPS and respond with a 2xx within 5 seconds. Each delivery is signed with the endpoint secret in the X-Signature header. The delivery log shows the last 500 attempts with request and response bodies.

title: Webhook retries and automatic disabling
text: Failed deliveries are retried with exponential backoff over 24 hours. An endpoint that fails 50 consecutive deliveries is automatically disabled and the workspace owner is emailed. Disabled endpoints must be re-enabled manually and do not receive events missed while disabled; use the Events API to backfill.

title: Managing and rotating API keys
text: Up to 10 keys can be active per workspace, so zero-downtime rotation is supported: create the new key, deploy it, then revoke the old one. Keys can be scoped to read-only. Revocation is immediate and cannot be undone. Key secrets are shown once at creation.

title: Cursor pagination
text: List endpoints return a next_cursor that is valid for 15 minutes. For exports larger than that, use the Export API which produces a downloadable file asynchronously, or store the cursor and resume promptly. Cursors are opaque and tied to the original filter parameters.

title: TLS requirements
text: The API requires TLS 1.2 or higher and uses a certificate chain rooted at a public CA. Corporate networks that perform TLS inspection replace our certificate with an internal one; the SDK will reject it unless the corporate root CA is added to the trust store or the proxy is configured to bypass api.* hosts.

title: SDK troubleshooting
text: Set the SDK log level to debug to see request IDs; include the request ID in any support ticket. Common issues: outdated SDK versions missing newer endpoints, proxy environment variables not honoured by the HTTP client, and system clocks off by more than 5 minutes causing signature failures.

title: Bulk endpoints
text: Bulk endpoints accept up to 500 ids per request. Ids that do not exist or that the key cannot access are omitted from the response rather than causing an error; check the returned count against the requested count. Requests above 500 ids return 400.

title: Exporting data
text: Exports from Settings > Data > Export include all fields visible to the exporting user. Custom fields and fields hidden by a saved view are included; fields the user lacks permission to see are not. Large exports run asynchronously and are emailed as a download link valid for 48 hours.

title: Data retention and soft delete
text: Deleted projects, items, and files are held in Trash for 30 days on all paid plans and 7 days on the free tier, then permanently removed. Workspace admins can restore anything in Trash. After the retention window, data is not recoverable from backups by support.

title: Restoring deleted items
text: Open Settings > Trash, locate the item, and click Restore. Restored items return to their original location with history intact. If the parent project was also deleted, restore the project first. Items older than the retention window no longer appear in Trash.

title: GDPR and data subject requests
text: Erasure, access, and portability requests are handled by the privacy team. Workspace admins can delete a member's personal data from Members > Remove and erase. Requests from data subjects directly, or for data across multiple workspaces, must be verified and are completed within 30 days as required by Article 12.

title: Importing from other tools
text: Native importers exist for Trello, Asana, Monday, Notion, and CSV. Start from Settings > Data > Import. Imports run in the background and email a summary. A failed job shows a reason in the job details panel; click the job id to expand it.

title: Import limits and common failures
text: Import files are limited to 250 MB and 100,000 rows. Common failures: attachments over 25 MB each, unsupported date formats in CSV, and source exports that were generated with a free-tier account missing fields. Split large files or remove oversized attachments and retry.

title: Data residency
text: Workspaces are hosted in the region selected at creation: US (Virginia), EU (Frankfurt), or AU (Sydney). Region cannot be changed after creation; a migration requires a new workspace and an export/import. Backups stay in the same region as the primary.

title: Backups
text: Full backups run daily and incremental backups every hour, encrypted at rest, retained for 35 days. Backups are for disaster recovery of the platform and are not used to restore individual customer deletions; use Trash for that. A signed backup and recovery statement is available on request for Enterprise customers.

title: Slack integration
text: Connect Slack from Settings > Integrations. Notification rules are per channel and per project. Duplicate messages usually mean the same project is subscribed by two rules, or the workspace was connected to Slack twice by different admins; check Integrations > Slack > Connected workspaces.

title: Integration catalog
text: Native integrations: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Calendar, Outlook, GitHub, GitLab, Jira, HubSpot, Salesforce (Enterprise), Zapier, and Make. Anything not listed can typically be connected through Zapier or the public API. Feature requests for new integrations are tracked on the public roadmap.

title: Zapier and Make
text: The Zapier app supports triggers for created and updated items and actions for create, update, and comment. Connect using an API key with the zapier scope. Zaps are billed by Zapier, not by us.

title: Google Calendar sync
text: Google Calendar sync is bidirectional for events created in either system after the integration was connected. Edits made in Google to events that originated here sync back within 5 minutes; if they do not, the integration's OAuth token has likely expired and must be reconnected.

title: GitHub integration
text: The GitHub app links commits and pull requests by reference. Install it on the GitHub organization, not on individual repositories, so new repositories are covered automatically. Migrating GitHub organizations or moving to GitHub Enterprise requires reinstalling the app on the new organization.

title: Reconnecting an integration
text: When an integration stops working after a change on the other side (new organization, password change, SSO enablement), go to Settings > Integrations, choose the integration, and click Reconnect. Existing mappings are kept.

title: Jira integration
text: Map each project to a Jira project under Settings > Integrations > Jira. Issue creation uses the mapping of the item's current project at the time of creation; items moved between projects keep their original Jira link. If issues appear in the wrong Jira project, verify that the Jira user connected has create permission in the target project.

title: Keyboard shortcuts
text: Press ? anywhere to see the shortcut cheat sheet. Shortcuts can be remapped from Settings > Preferences.

title: Mobile apps
text: iOS and Android apps support offline editing with sync on reconnect. Push notifications follow the same rules as email notifications.

title: Service status
text: Live status and incident history are published on the status page. Subscribe by email or RSS for incident updates.

title: Plan comparison
text: Starter, Pro, Team, Business, and Enterprise differ in seats, storage, SSO availability, API limits, and audit log retention. See the pricing page for the full matrix.

title: Project templates
text: Templates capture a project's structure and can be shared across the workspace. Marketplace templates are community-contributed.

title: Appearance and themes
text: Dark mode follows the system setting by default and can be forced in Settings > Preferences > Appearance.

title: Notification settings
text: Email digests, real-time email, and in-app notifications are configured independently per workspace under Settings > Notifications.

title: Accessibility
text: The web app is WCAG 2.1 AA compliant, supports screen readers, and exposes all actions via keyboard.
